chapter.title: Loop
chapter.sub: A student has heard half of every lecture through the hearing loop — and blamed her own ears.
chapter.status: **DRAFT** · scripted from the series plan · IDs provisional

items.text: SEASON 5 · EPISODE 3 · DRAFT · CASE-027  Accessibility · Farah, Maya and Mira · Level L4 · Intermediate support  A student has heard half of every lecture for a semester through Hall B’s hearing loop — and blamed her own ears. The sign on the door promised her everything.  ⚑ RV-126: loop figures simplified. RV-123: access is a right. Some choices run on a clock.

items.title: Row Ten
items.stakes: A student has heard half of every lecture for a semester and blamed her own ears. The sign on the door promised her everything.
items.clock: Before the 10:55 lecture — and for the rest of the semester.
items.reward: Every seat in Hall B within reach of the loop, proven by the people who use it. Farah's trust. An honest sign.

objectives.text: Give Mira what she needs today
Find out what PASS really meant
Look closer: two things about row ten

items.rumor: The loop was fine in July. Something changed under the seats.

items.alt: Hall B, empty before the lecture. The blue hearing-loop sign hangs by the door. Farah and Maya stand at the front.

bubbles.text: The sign's been up since July. It says everyone with a telecoil hears every word.

lines.text: She said she thought her hearing was getting worse. She's booked an audiologist.

items.alt: Hall B from the lectern: Farah points up the left side of the tiered seating toward row 10, near the side exit.

bubbles.text: Row ten, left side, by the exit. She always sits there.

items.caption: Near the door. On purpose.

items.prompt: Do we tell her to sit at the front? It'd be easier.

options.label: “Easier for us. Let's offer her a receiver today and make the room reach her seat.”
options.reply: That's the answer I've been waiting three years for someone in AV to give.

options.label: “Yes, just for now.”
options.reply: She sits by the exit for a reason. She shouldn't have to explain it to us.

options.label: “Let's ask her what she'd prefer.”
options.reply: Good. She'll pick the receiver — and she'll stay by the door.

items.text: ✦ UX RULE #44 · AVERY'S LENS  A sign is a promise  Accessibility signs must be true for every seat they cover — or say honestly where they aren't, and what to do instead.  Hall B's loop sign promised everyone. Rows 8–12 got half a lecture.

items.prompt: 10:40. Mira's lecture starts at 10:55 and she'll be in row 10 again. What do you do before then?
known: ◉ Loop signed off PASS in July
items.risk: Another lecture she'll only half hear.
timeout: 10:55 comes. Mira sits in row 10 and writes half-pages again.
Fifteen minutes was enough for a receiver.

hints.text: What can she have in fifteen minutes that doesn't depend on the loop?

options.label: Ask Mira to sit in the front row today
options.result: She moves, quietly. Farah tells you later that she sits by the exit for a reason she shouldn't have to explain.
options.consequence: It works for one lecture and asks her to fix our room.

options.label: Offer Mira a portable receiver today — her choice — and investigate the room
options.result: She takes it. Ten minutes in she whispers to Farah: “Oh. That's what he sounds like.”
options.consequence: An alternative now, her decision, and the room still gets fixed.

options.label: Turn the loop amplifier to maximum
options.result: The front rows distort, and the loop in Hall C next door starts carrying Hall B's lecture.
options.consequence: More current everywhere breaks the places that worked.
options.fail: Turning it up doesn't fix a zone — it breaks the others.

options.label: Nothing until you've measured
options.consequence: Measurement can wait fifteen minutes; she can't.

items.alt: The acceptance record: one measurement at front center, 410 mA/m, PASS. Other seats: none. Listening test: none.
items.caption: PASS, measured once, in an empty room, in July.

items.title: One line
items.body: *Loop field, front center: 410 mA/m. PASS.* One reading, one seat, one July afternoon, the room empty. Nobody walked to row 10. Maya adds a page to the template: a grid of every row, and a line for *listening test by telecoil users — names and seats.*

items.title: PASS was one point.
items.body: The whole acceptance test was a single reading at front center. Nobody measured row 10, and nobody who uses a telecoil was ever asked to listen. PASS proved one seat.
items.label: Test: what does PASS rule out — and what should it have included?

items.sub: Intermediate · the skill behind this chapter

items.alt: A teaching moment: Farah and Maya beside a board. The loop's level is twenty log of H over H-ref. H is what the meter reads in that seat; H-ref is the target, four hundred milliamps per metre. Row ten reads a hundred. A quarter of the target — minus twelve dB. Minus twelve dB is a student who hears nothing and assumes it's her.

bubbles.text: The loop's level is twenty log of H over H-ref. H is what the meter reads in that seat; H-ref is the target, four hundred milliamps per metre.
Row ten reads a hundred. A quarter of the target — minus twelve dB.
Minus twelve dB is a student who hears nothing and assumes it's her.

items.caption: Intermediate: the formula and what every letter means. The arithmetic is yours.

items.text: 📗 FIELD NOTES · INTERMEDIATE  Terms   Hearing loop   Field strength   Dead zone   Formula and variables   ƒ FORMULA · Hearing-loop field level  L = 20·log 10 (H ÷ H ref )   H  measured magnetic field strength, mA/m  H ref   reference field, 400 mA/m (illustrative target)  L  level relative to the reference, dB     ƒ FORMULA · Level difference  ΔL = L 1  − L 2    L 1   the higher level, dB  L 2   the lower level, dB

items.label: **Learn it now:** hearing loops — field, coverage and honest signs.

items.prompt: 2:00 p.m. Hall B is free. How do you find out where the loop fails?
unknown: The shape of the dead zone
timeout: The room fills at 4:00 before anyone measures.
Surveys need an empty room — you had one.

hints.text: What would turn 'about half' into a map?

options.label: Walk the room with a field-strength meter and map every row
options.result: Rows 1–7 near reference. Rows 8–12, left: about −12 dB. A clean rectangle of red.
options.consequence: Every seat is its own proof.

options.label: Put up a form asking students to report problems
options.result: Two replies by Friday — both from the front.
options.consequence: The people it fails most rarely report.

options.label: Listen yourself with the receiver
options.result: You hear it fine at the front and faintly at row 10 — no numbers, no map.

items.title: Sound carried by a magnetic field
items.body: In 1937 the British engineer Joseph Poliakoff patented an audio induction loop: a wire that turns sound into a magnetic field a listening device can pick up. Hearing aids later gained telecoils to receive it. The idea is almost a century old; what fails is rarely the physics — it's whether anyone measured every seat.

items.alt: A field-strength map of Hall B, twelve rows by fourteen seats: green almost everywhere, a red rectangle over rows 8–12 on the left, outlined as the steel platform added in September.
items.caption: A rectangle. Rooms don't fail in rectangles. Buildings do.

items.alt: Maya and Wes at the side of Hall B; a floor panel is already open (by facilities) showing the steel frame of the platform extension under rows 8–12.

bubbles.text: Steel frame. Added in September for the robotics team. After the loop.
So the loop was fine when they tested it.

lines.text: How did a steel platform get under a hearing loop?
The same way everything does. Someone needed a platform. Nobody asked the loop.

items.title: The platform came later.
items.body: Facilities' log: a steel-framed platform extension under rows 8–12, installed in September for the robotics team — two months after the loop passed. Nobody re-tested the loop, because nobody connected a platform to a hearing aid.
items.label: Test: what changed, and who approves the fix?
**Fix it:** get the loop to row 10.

items.alt: Thursday evening after the installer's work: Farah sits in row 10 with a telecoil receiver while Maya reads a sentence from the lectern.

bubbles.text: Clear. Clearer than the front used to be.
Now Mira and two more volunteers, in rows eight to twelve.

items.prompt: Friday. What should acceptance of a hearing loop mean from now on?
unknown: The next change under the seats
items.risk: The same dead zone in another hall.
timeout: The acceptance template stays one line long.
Next summer's loops will pass the same way.

hints.text: What would have caught September's platform?

options.label: A seat-by-seat field map, a telecoil listening test with users, both in the file — and a re-test after any change near the seating
options.result: Facilities adds a line to its change form: ‘metal near assistive-listening systems? → AV re-test.’
options.consequence: PASS means the people it's for can hear.

options.label: A second reading at the back
Trust the installer's paperwork
options.fail: PASS without a map is a claim.

options.label: Remove the loop sign so nobody is misled
options.result: Telecoil users lose the one clue that a room supports them.
options.consequence: Removing the promise instead of keeping it.

items.label: **Sequence:** commission a loop you can trust.
**Service Mode:** run Tuesday in Hall B yourself.

items.alt: The field map after the repair: every seat in Hall B green, within ±3 dB of the reference.
items.caption: Every seat, not one.

items.alt: Hall B's new sign: HEARING LOOP — every seat, tested with users. Farah and Maya beside it.

bubbles.text: Mira cancelled the audiologist. Her ears were fine. Our room wasn't.

items.title: Half-pages
items.body: Mira's lecture notes, which she shows Farah later: full pages until row 10, then half-pages with gaps and question marks. At the top of one: *ask audiologist — worse on Tuesdays?* Tuesdays are Hall B.

items.alt: The AV operations office; a handful of room tiles blink red. Wes on the phone; Officer Delgado, the campus security lead, standing in the doorway.

bubbles.text: Exam week. The ceiling mics in the proctored rooms keep rebooting mid-exam.
So do my new cameras. Same rooms. Same minute.

items.caption: Next: *Exam Week.*

items.text: FIELD NOTE —  A hearing loop proves itself two ways: a seat-by-seat field map and a listening test by the people who use it. Re-test after anything metal changes near the seating, keep signs honest, and give people an alternative today — their choice.
REFLECTION (optional)  · Mira blamed her own ears before anyone checked the room. What would make it easier for people to report that a room isn’t working for them?
